PullRequest.Title: Add experimental settings for Auto's tiers and Intelligence routing
PullRequest.Body:
Stacked on #340895.

Adds two experiment-controlled settings for local Copilot Agent Host sessions:
- `chat.copilot.ensemble.enabled`: presents Auto under a new name with Balance, Intelligence, and Max (HydraFusion Max), dropping Efficiency. Turns on HydraFusion v2, which Max needs, unless HydraFusion is off.
- `chat.copilot.ensemble.intelligenceUsesHydraFusion`: with the first setting on, Intelligence uses HydraFusion v2, falling back to normal Intelligence routing when HydraFusion is unavailable.

The picker, chat input, and response footers name the selected tier. Both settings log experiment triggers in every arm.

Scenarios.Scenario: Local Copilot Agent Host startup, settings synchronization, and model catalog publication
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Agent-host enablement starts the root-config forwarder; values that differ from hydrated root state cross the local agent-host protocol before the host observes them. Existing model enumeration must complete before the catalog is published. Ensemble metadata transformation is synchronous after enumeration. A user setting transition that enables HydraFusion v2 can require the existing Copilot client to restart once all active turns are idle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch Ensemble and EnsembleIntelligenceUsesHydraFusion root-config values to the local agent host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two newly managed key dispatches during initial reconciliation when host values differ; later only on relevant setting/policy transitions. Ensemble also recomputes HydraFusionV2, but equality gating suppresses unchanged values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two keys were not forwarded; existing settings already used one equality-gated IPC action per key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial differing values must reach the host before host-side routing metadata reflects them; otherwise the dispatch is absent from the critical path. The two messages are bounded and not collection-scaled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restart the Copilot SDK client when Ensemble makes HydraFusion v2 effective
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one deferred/coalesced restart for a relevant explicit setting transition; no restart per model or turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: HydraFusion v2 changes already caused this restart; enabling Ensemble can now make v2 effective when HydraFusion v1 is enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A deliberate setting transition may delay the next session until restart/model refresh; active turns are explicitly allowed to finish first.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List runtime models through the existing Copilot client
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing model-list request per scheduled refresh, with existing retry and in-flight control; the metadata transformation does not add requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same refresh enumerated models before publishing them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing boundary before model availability; the diff only filters/maps its returned catalog.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two new root-config keys; model publication scales linearly with the effective CAPI catalog, normally tens of models. Host root-config handling also inspects existing sessions, but the added actions are constant-cardinality and settings changes are rare.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The forwarder evaluates each key independently and equality-gates dispatches. Model refreshes use the existing in-flight scheduling/retry mechanism. Client restart requests are deferred around active work and coalesced through pending restart state rather than launched concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm root state suppresses structurally equal key dispatches. The fetched CAPI catalog remains in _capiModels and is transformed in memory on publication; no new model-list cache miss is introduced. Empty/error model refresh behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that two bounded IPC keys and a possible intentional setting-transition restart are added; high confidence no per-model boundary fan-out is added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact local IPC and restart duration varies by machine and catalog size, but cardinality and restart coalescing are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added work is bounded, equality-gated, and tied to startup or explicit experiment-setting transitions rather than a hot interaction path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, rendering, and changing the model picker with Ensemble/HydraFusion tiers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the picker synchronously scans the already-loaded model list, builds destinations/cards, and renders DOM. Selection normalization runs when the selected-model observable or entitlement changes. Telemetry logging is synchronous but globally deduplicated; a compatibility config update is launched asynchronously and does not block normalization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one telemetry event per window for the treatment despite repeated opens, selection normalization, or history use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No trigger for this new setting existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first call performs a single telemetry-service submission while opening or normalizing; subsequent calls return from the in-memory Set.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist Ensemble's Intelligence tier when moving a chat off HydraFusion
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical edit for the transition; per-model sequencing and ChatModelConfigurationStore equality checks suppress repeated no-op profile writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The promise is not awaited by selection normalization, so persistence is off the immediate UI critical path; local selection switches immediately.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective model-list cardinality, typically tens; tier choices and routing alternatives are bounded to a few entries. Added list scans are O(models), while card merge work is over two tiers and up to two routing alternatives.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model configuration edits are serialized per model with SequencerByKey. The editor-scoped configuration store suppresses no-op persistence; telemetry triggers are deduplicated per telemetry service/window.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Models and configuration schemas are in memory. Per-editor model configuration is cached after first read; no-op writes are suppressed. Experiment-trigger state is retained in a WeakMap for the window, making later picker opens warm/no-op.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the UI call paths, telemetry deduplication, per-model sequencer, and persistence no-op guard from direct implementation inspection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Model counts and DOM render time vary, but routing alternatives are fixed and the new scans do not alter asymptotic picker behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Synchronous additions are small in-memory scans over an already-rendered catalog; boundary work is once-per-window or transition-only and coalesced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restoring an agent-host chat and rendering response footers for Ensemble tiers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing session/chat subscriptions hydrate over the agent-host connection; then completed turns are converted once into history before the chat is returned. Each turn already scans its response parts to determine routing; the diff adds in-memory model lookup/label formatting and may call the deduplicated trigger.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hydrate session and chat state from the local agent host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same existing session and chat subscription hydration per restored chat; no new subscription is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restoration already awaited both subscriptions and converted every turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing prerequisite before history conversion; added footer formatting runs only after hydration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the Intelligence-routing experiment trigger while formatting a qualifying footer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Although invoked from per-turn conversion, logSettingExperimentTrigger emits at most one event per telemetry service/window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Footer conversion did not trigger this new experiment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: One bounded first-use telemetry submission can occur during history conversion; later qualifying turns only perform a Set membership check.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of restored turns T and response parts per turn. The added footer work remains O(T), with constant-size schema lookup per Fusion turn. Effective telemetry boundary cardinality is one per window, not one per turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hydration subscriptions are awaited as before. History is explicitly built once. No added parallel network or filesystem work is launched per turn.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Language-model metadata is already registered/in memory. The first qualifying Intelligence turn warms the experiment-trigger Set; all later turns and sessions are no-op for telemetry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence because provideChatSessionContent states history is built once and experimentTrigger.ts enforces per-window treatment deduplication.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long histories increase existing O(T) conversion cost, but the changed per-turn operations are small and the only boundary is globally deduplicated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds constant in-memory footer work per turn and no per-turn IPC/network fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launching or resuming an Auto/Ensemble session with a saved tier
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before the existing SDK session creation boundary, the launcher resolves the configured override or picker tier and performs one additional root-config read only when the tier is Efficiency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or resume the Copilot SDK session using resolved session options
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing session creation/resume operation per session; the diff does not add another call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session boundary received the saved Efficiency tier without Ensemble normalization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing critical boundary; the new tier conversion is constant CPU work before it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected model/tier per session launch; no collection multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new asynchronous work or parallelism. Existing session creation sequencing is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Root configuration is in-memory; cold/warm behavior is identical apart from the constant lookup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the synchronous helper and unchanged launcher boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: SDK session creation latency varies externally, but changed code adds no boundary call or wait.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added work is a single in-memory setting lookup and log decision per relevant launch.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 26 changed files and every diff page. Traced startup/root-config IPC, Copilot subprocess/model refresh behavior, picker render and persistence paths, telemetry deduplication, restored-history hydration, and session launch. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
